text: Amazing! thanks! /hand-over and the next thing they are going t o pick up on is setting pivot points for a layer, this pivot point is going to also require  joints. so like the center of a wheel is a pivot point, and then the location in the wheelbase of t he model, is the joint. this lets us put pivots inside of things that will rotate like shoulders, or tires. and their joint locations.
resolution: Studio pivot points + joints (Part 6, the 'rig' mode). Confirmed the user's asymmetric model side-by-side: pivot lives on the CHILD (rotation origin + upstream connection point), joint lives on the PARENT and owns the spin axis AND rotation limit (e.g. shoulder -90..+90 = 180 deg of travel, or full for tires); a part can be both and they nest (wheel = pivot on the body's axle joint + its own joint for a spinner). Data layer (editMesh.ts): EditMesh.pivot?:V3 (absent=bounds center, sticky once set like uv), MountPoint.limit + jointTravelDegrees, pure helpers meshBoundsCenter/pivotOf/setPivot/addMount/updateMount/removeMount. Persistence + undo came free by folding pivot+mounts onto EditMesh so they ride the existing partMeshUpdated event (zero new stream/studioModel code). Viewport: a 5th toolbar mode (object/vertex/edge/face/rig) with meshRig.tsx overlay (pivot crosshair-ball + joint rings with axis arrow + type/travel label), reusing the existing TransformGizmo + drag/snap/readout machinery; + joint button, RigJointPanel for type/kind/axis/limit, Delete removes a joint, Esc deselects. editMesh 40/40, modelStream 7/7, Studio + full sources chain bundle clean; hot-reload TSX, uncommitted per the user's lead. Spec in PLAYBOOK Part 6; memory project_studio_mesh_editor updated.
